payload.claim: When the salvage turn itself raises `implement.AgentFailed` (its own idle/wall-clock bound, or its own 5-turn `error_max_turns`), the handler only records `_failed_turn(failed, session_id)` and re-measures `commits_ahead` — it never falls back to `worktree.commit_dirty`, the host-side checkpoint the REPAIR loop's own `AgentFailed` handler applies a few lines below (session.py:1198-1202) for the identical situation (a bound firing leaving real edits uncommitted). If the salvage turn is itself cut off before it manages to `git commit`, the dirty tree it was resumed specifically to save is lost the same way the original SA-0025 run lost it, and this exact branch is untested (all three scripted `_drive` tests give the salvage turn a clean `_turn()` or a clean AgentFailed on the *first* implement turn, never an AgentFailed on the salvage turn itself).
